hooks.prompt:
A file was just edited or written. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

Parse that JSON. Get the file path from tool_input.file_path (fall back to tool_response.filePath if absent). If there is no file path, the file doesn't exist, or it isn't a source code file (e.g. it's markdown, JSON, YAML, a lockfile, or a binary/image), produce no output and stop.

Read the file. Find every comment in it (//, /* */, #, <!-- -->, docstrings — whatever the language uses). If the file has no comments, produce no output and stop.

Judge each comment against this project's comment policy (from CLAUDE.md):
- A comment must carry RATIONALE, not narration. If it only restates what the next line or block already does, it fails — the fix is a better name or a split, not the comment.
- A comment is warranted only when the reason is invisible from the code itself: a browser/runtime quirk, a spec requirement, a deliberately non-obvious approach, or a constraint that would look like a mistake to the next reader.
- Commented-out code, changelog-style comments ("added for X", "fixes #123", "used by the Y flow"), section-banner comments, and multi-line/docstring comment blocks always fail — one short line, only when the why is non-obvious, is the ceiling.

If every comment already satisfies this (or there are none), produce no output and stop — do not praise or summarize, just stay silent.

If one or more comments fail, respond with exactly one line of JSON and nothing else — no code fences, no prose before or after it:
{"decision":"block","reason":"<one bullet per flagged comment: file:line, the comment text, why it fails, and what to do instead>"}
hooks.statusMessage: Re-checking whether comments in the touched file are still necessary...
